gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 diagnoses an incorrect projection identity and density assumption for F-F_N#, whereas the gold defect is the missing factor ||x|| when bounding (I-P_N)F x over a ball. Its repair does not identify this failed norm estimate.
Both identify the invalid transfer from H^s-continuity plus C-compactness to the C-supremum continuity required by finite point-sampling approximants, for both functional and operator statements.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The approximation architectures are continuous in the input supremum topology, but the hypotheses provide only H^s-continuity; compact Sobolev embedding does not supply the missing C-continuity.

component_coverage.gold_component: The functional and operator approximation theorems use point-sampling maps continuous in the C-supremum topology while assuming only H^s-continuity, so the claimed uniform approximation is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 explicitly states the topology mismatch, gives scalar and L²-valued counterexamples, and proposes replacing H^s-continuity with C-continuity or H^s-compactness.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-007 identifies a boundary-specific mollification leaving D(F), but does not diagnose the general requirement that the whole local ball and every M_xi x remain in D(F). The gold therefore has an unrecognised domain-admissibility obligation.

ISSUE-007 concerns boundary-layer mollification rates and preservation of a constrained domain. It does not identify the false same-radius localization M_xi(B_r(x*)) subset of B_r(x*) or the missing control of displacement from x*.

ISSUE-008 explicitly identifies that the theorem chooses xi and one network before quantifying over every center, while the proof constructs them after fixing a center, and its repair makes center dependence explicit.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem asserts a single finite network and smoothing scale uniformly for all centers, but the proof only supports center-dependent choices.

component_coverage.gold_component: The global quantifier order requires one network to approximate at every center, while the proof establishes only a center-dependent local approximation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the quantifier-order inconsistency and explicitly repairs it by making xi and network parameters depend on the selected center and epsilon.
